title: Goal Programming Model in Financial Planning of the International Development Bank
tldr: A weighted-preemptive hybrid Goal Programming model optimized seven competing financial objectives for an Iraqi bank from 2016 to 2024, achieving near-optimal solutions with minimal deviations using WINQSB.
problem_and_motivation: Financial institutions face complex decision-making challenges from multiple conflicting objectives such as profitability, cost control, and liquidity. Traditional financial planning models struggle to accommodate these competing goals, especially in developing economies with resource constraints. Goal Programming application in the financial sector of emerging markets like Iraq remains underexplored.
approach: Financial data from IDB annual reports spanning 2016-2024 were collected and scaled to billion Iraqi dinars.
Seven competing financial objectives were formulated as constraints: revenue, expenses, net profit, fixed assets, loans, common stock, and financial management ratio.
A weighted-preemptive hybrid Goal Programming model was developed combining priority ranking with assigned deviation weights.
The model was solved using WINQSB optimization software to find near-optimal solutions.
Positive and negative deviations from target values were analyzed to evaluate goal achievement across all seven objectives.

num: Financial management ratio can be increased by 1.608461 billion annually with positive deviation of 1.1655.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: The paper introduces a weighted-preemptive hybrid Goal Programming framework that combines priority ranking with deviation weights for multi-objective financial optimization. It demonstrates the application of this technique in the banking sector of an emerging market, providing a case study with nine years of financial data. The study validates that near-optimal solutions can be achieved across seven competing financial objectives simultaneously. The framework offers a decision-support methodology for institutions balancing profitability, cost control, liquidity, and capital structure under resource constraints.

topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains in the taxonomy were systematically scanned. The paper was flagged as relevant to Domain 7 (Budgeting Strategies and Recommendation) because it applies Goal Programming, a constrained optimization technique, to financial resource allocation. Topic 7.C (Constrained Optimization Approaches for Budget Allocation) was assigned medium relevance as the GP framework directly demonstrates constrained optimization for financial objectives. Topic 4.B (Limitations and Gaps in Existing Systems) was assigned low relevance because the paper contextualizes traditional financial planning limitations as background motivation. Domains 1-3 (Filipino demographics, cultural finance, expense categorization) were rejected as the paper addresses institutional banking, not personal finance. Domains 5-6 (behavioral profiles, predictive modeling) were rejected as the paper uses deterministic optimization, not ML or behavioral analysis. Domain 8 (anomaly detection), Domain 9 (mobile design), Domain 10 (privacy), Domain 11 (engagement), Domain 13 (savings/debt), and Domain 14 (ML/synthetic data) were rejected as wholly unrelated. Domain 12.B was considered but deemed too tangential for inclusion. The paper's topical coverage centers on constrained optimization methodology applied to institutional financial planning.
